newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stockholm divers find gun but not one shot Palme.
newsitem.headline: Stockholm divers find gun but not one shot Palme.

text.p: A private team of divers searching a lake in Stockholm for the weapon used to kill former Swedish prime minister Olof Palme have found a gun but it was not the murder weapon, police said on Friday.
"Our technicians are investigating it but it's not the same kind of gun we are looking for," Detective Superintendent Per-Olov Palmgren said.
The divers found a small pistol, not the Smith & Wesson .357 Magnum revolver used to shoot Palme as he returned home from the cinema with his wife on February 28, 1986.
"It seems to be a smaller pistol so it's not interesting for us," Palmgren said.

The Swedish-Norwegian team has also pulled about 150 cartridges from the five-metre (16-foot) deep floor of the Klara Sjo (Lake Klara) where the murder weapon may have been thrown after the assassination, Swedish media reports said.
The search for the gun that killed Palme, codenamed Operation .357, started on Wednesday this week.
Two Norwegian companies are financing the project, estimated to cost between 500,000 crowns ($65,000) and one million, in part to test a new technique that uses sound waves to detect metal objects.
Donald Forsberg, a Swedish diver leading the operation, said he believed the murder weapon must be there. A 50 million crown reward has been offered to help solve the murder.

The search is focusing on the Klara Sjo because of the testimony of Swedish underworld figure, Lars Tingstrom, known as the Bomb Man, who claimed in a 1993 deathbed confession that he was part of a gang of four involved in the murder.

His lawyer, Pelle Svensson, said Tingstrom claimed the gang also included Christer Pettersson, who was convicted of Palme's murder in 1988 but later acquitted, as well as a former bank robber and an explosives expert, now dead.
